L313: ## Remote control for people
L314: 
L315: The same daemon that serves agents lets you drive the phone yourself:
L316:   * From a browser. The live screen arrives as H.264 encoded on the phone: native resolution at about 50 fps on the LAN, and a lighter mode for slow links. Click to tap, drag to swipe, hold to long-press, scroll with the wheel or trackpad. Type straight into the phone with your input method, and ⌘V pastes. The Controls panel lists the screen's elements so you can tap by label, and the Flow panel records what you do as a replayable flow.
L317: The page follows your browser's language (English or Chinese), with a switch in the sidebar.
L318:   * From another iPhone. The native iOS app (minimum deployment target iOS 15) pairs by scanning a QR code on the Mac's page, with no address or password to type. It plays the screen with the hardware decoder and switches between your phones. Install it with `iphone-use setup-app`, which signs it with your own team; with a paid team the app also controls its own phone with no Mac (【124†details】).
L319:   * Screens hidden from capture. Banking and payment apps black out screen capture; there you see a live wireframe of the screen's elements instead of a blank picture, and you can still tap through it.
L320:   * From anywhere. Reach the Mac through an authenticated HTTPS reverse proxy or a VPN such as Tailscale, and control the phone from outside your network (【125†security notes】).
L321:   * No collisions. A phone has one owner at a time. While you are in control, an agent waits or is told who holds the phone, and the reverse is true too.
L322: Nothing on the Mac moves while you do it: no window takes focus and the cursor stays put.
L323: ## Use it from an agent
L324: 
L325: To save a screenshot on the phone for use in another app, call `phone_shortcut {"name":"save_screenshot"}`. It requests an iOS system capture in Photos; check the new image before claiming it saved. `phone_screenshot` returns an image to the caller. Saving requires an updated native Runner.
L326: 
L327: A daemon on your Mac drives the phone and offers the same control in three forms:
L328:   * an MCP server for Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients;
L329:   * an HTTP API for agents and scripts (`/agent/*`);
L330:   * a web page and a native iOS app for people (【123†remote control】).
L331: The installer registers the MCP server with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Claude Desktop when they are present (`IPHONE_USE_NO_CLIENT_SETUP=1` leaves Cursor and Claude Desktop alone). Any other MCP client needs only the command; on this Mac the server finds the daemon and its token by itself:
L332: 
L333:     {
L334:       "mcpServers": {
L335:         "iphone-use": {
L336:           "command": "/Users/YOU/Applications/iPhoneUse.app/Contents/MacOS/iphone-use-mcp"
L337:         }
L338:       }
L339:     }
L340: Config for Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop, Gemini CLI, opencode, Windsurf
L341: 
L342: Use the absolute path (replace `YOU`) and merge the entry into the file; keep the servers already there.
L343: 
L344:   * Cursor: `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (or `.cursor/mcp.json` in a project), the `mcpServers` block above.
L345: 
L346:   * Claude Desktop: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`, the `mcpServers` block above; quit and reopen the app.
L347:   * Gemini CLI: `~/.gemini/settings.json` (or `.gemini/settings.json` in a project), the `mcpServers` block above.
L348: 
L349:   * Windsurf / Devin Desktop: `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` (newer builds: `~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json`), the `mcpServers` block above.
L350:   * VS Code / Copilot: `.vscode/mcp.json` in a workspace, or MCP: Open User Configuration for every workspace. The key is `servers`:
L351: 
L352:     {
L353:       "servers": {
L354:         "iphone-use": {
L355:           "type": "stdio",
L356:           "command": "/Users/YOU/Applications/iPhoneUse.app/Contents/MacOS/iphone-use-mcp"
L357:         }
L358:       }
L359:     }
L360:   * opencode: `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (or `opencode.json` in a project). The key is `mcp` and the command is an array:
L361: 
L362:     {
L363:       "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
L364:       "mcp": {
L365:         "iphone-use": {
L366:           "type": "local",
L367:           "command": ["/Users/YOU/Applications/iPhoneUse.app/Contents/MacOS/iphone-use-mcp"],
L368:           "enabled": true
L369:         }
L370:       }
L371:     }
L372: Or call the HTTP API directly:
L373: 
L374:     AUTH="Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"; CTL="X-Phone-Control: 1"
L375:     curl -s -H "$AUTH" $HOST/agent/elements                     # the screen as text + a snapshot token
L376:     curl -s -H "$AUTH" -H "$CTL" -X POST "$HOST/agent/input?return=delta" \
L377:       -d '{"type":"tap","element":7,"snapshot":"…"}'            # tap, then what changed (~2 s)
L378: For app developers and testers the same tools also read the phone's logs and crash reports, record the screen to MP4, install a build (`.ipa`, `.app` or an https link), set a simulated location, and keep per-app notes that agents read when they enter the app. `IPHONE_USE_MCP_TOOLS=readonly` exposes only the tools that read, and `iphone-use-mcp --listen 127.0.0.1:PORT` serves MCP over HTTP.
L379: A loopback listener is reachable only from the same Mac; for a client on another machine, put it behind an authenticated tunnel, or listen on another address with `IPHONE_USE_MCP_TOKEN` set (it is required off loopback).
L380: No phone at hand? While you develop, drive an iOS Simulator the same way (preview, needs Xcode): `iphone-use simulator start "iPhone 16 Pro"` builds and starts everything, then point the agent at it with `claude mcp add iphone-sim -e IPHONE_USE_INSTANCE=sim -- iphone-use-mcp`. See 【126†Simulators】.
L381: 
L382: See the 【127†MCP tools】 and the 【128†Agent API reference】.
L383: ## Safety and privacy
L384:   * Secrets stay with you. For logins, passcodes and Face ID the agent stops and asks you to finish on the phone. It never asks for the password or the code.
L385:   * Limits the agent cannot talk its way past. The daemon refuses apps you block (`IPHONE_USE_BLOCKED_APPS`, for example `Wallet, Passwords`) and caps the actions per task (`IPHONE_USE_MAX_ACTIONS`), whatever the agent's prompt says (【129†details】).
L386:   * You see what it does. The web page shows each action over the live screen in plain words, for example `Tapped “Wi-Fi”`. Typed text is never kept, only its length.
L387:   * Local by default. The daemon listens on `127.0.0.1:44321` behind a password, and the runner on the phone accepts only requests signed with a per-launch token. The iOS 15/16 LAN path is unencrypted (【125†security】).
L388:   * No telemetry. This build sends no usage data (【130†telemetry】 · 【131†privacy policy】).
L389: `phone_home_layout` reads the paired phone's persisted home pages, Dock, folders and widget stacks without opening folders or taking screenshots. Use `page` to limit the response. Its page indexes include hidden/Focus-filtered pages; use fresh UI elements before dragging, rather than treating grid slots as screen coordinates.
L390: ## Flows: do a task once, replay it with no model
L391: 
L392: Tasks you repeat are kept as flows: reviewed per-app scripts that replay without a model, so they cost no tokens. The official registry is 【132†leeguooooo/iphone-use-flows】. Record a flow in the browser's Flow panel and publish it there with a PR.
L393: Agents find flows on their own: when one enters an app, the response lists that app's flows. After an agent does a multi-step task in an app that has none, it asks whether to save the task as a flow; the daemon has already recorded the steps as a draft. The daemon keeps the registry fresh by itself (`IPHONE_USE_FLOWS_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` turns that off, `IPHONE_USE_FLOWS_NO_SUGGEST=1` silences the save suggestions).
L394: 
L395:     MCP=~/Applications/iPhoneUse.app/Contents/MacOS/iphone-use-mcp
L396:     $MCP flow update                            # sync the registry (sha256-checked)
L397:     $MCP flow list                              # what is available
L398:     $MCP flow run health/export-all-zh-cn       # replay one; failures say which step and why
L399:     $MCP flow draft --out my-task.json          # what you just did on the phone, as a draft flow
L400: Flows also make rerunnable test suites (`$MCP test suite.yaml`, with an exit code ready for CI) and scheduled runs the daemon starts on a cron line (`$MCP schedule add`): see 【133†Testing and scheduled runs】.
L401: ## Speed
L402: 
L403: iphone-use drives the phone through its own XCTest runner (【134†`runner/`】). It speaks the WebDriverAgent HTTP API, and it is built for speed:
L404:   * It reads the screen with one accessibility snapshot of a fixed attribute set, instead of walking the element tree attribute by attribute.
L405:   * It synthesizes touches directly and does not wait for the app to go idle before acting; the daemon checks afterwards that the screen has settled.
L406:   * It is one small app with a built-in HTTP server and MJPEG stream; there are no extra dependencies on the phone.
L407: 
L408: Measured on the same iPhone 13 over USB, against 【135†agent-device】 (October 2026):
L409:  | iphone-use runner  | agent-device
L410: --- | --- | ---
L411: Read the screen (accessibility tree)  | 0.08–0.135 s  | ~0.7 s
L412: Tap, then wait for the screen to settle  | 1.0 s  | 2.8–3.3 s
L413: 
L414: Through the full agent API, a tap by label that returns the settled change takes about 1.9 s on an iPhone 17 Pro Max; the WebDriverAgent-based release took 4.2 s. The live view streams at 27–28 fps. Each phone gets its own daemon and runner, so two phones driven at the same time run as fast as either one alone.

# Installing iphone-use (for AI agents)

These are the steps an AI agent follows to install iphone-use on the user's Mac and register its MCP
server. iphone-use is a macOS app with a daemon, not an npm or pip package: there is nothing to
`npx`, and the MCP server only works on the Mac the iPhone is plugged into.

## Requirements (check before you start)

- macOS 15 or later (`sw_vers -productVersion`). On any other OS, stop and tell the user.
- Xcode installed and signed in to an Apple ID (a free one works). Only the user can sign in.
- An iPhone with iOS 15 or later, Developer Mode on, plugged in by USB and unlocked for the first setup.

## Steps

1. Install. Run in a terminal on the Mac:

   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leeguooooo/iphone-use/main/install.sh | sh
   ```

   The installer puts the app at `~/Applications/iPhoneUse.app`, the CLI on the PATH as
   `iphone-use`, sets the phone up when one is plugged in, and registers the MCP server with
   Claude Code (`claude mcp add-json -s user iphone-use …`) and Codex (`codex mcp add iphone-use …`)
   when those CLIs are present.

2. Diagnose. Run `iphone-use doctor`. Fix what it reports that can be fixed from the terminal, and run
   `iphone-use setup` when it tells you to.

3. Hand the user what only they can do: signing in to an Apple ID in Xcode, tapping Trust on the
   iPhone, turning on Developer Mode, unlocking the phone. Stop, tell them exactly what to do, and wait
   until they say it is done. Never ask for a password, a passcode or a verification code.

4. Repeat `iphone-use doctor` until nothing is missing, then run `iphone-use try` (opens Settings,
   reads the screen, goes Home).

5. Register the MCP server with any other client. The command is the same everywhere and needs no
   arguments, env or token; on this Mac it finds the daemon and its token by itself:

   ```text
   /Users/<user>/Applications/iPhoneUse.app/Contents/MacOS/iphone-use-mcp
   ```

   Use the absolute path (expand `$HOME`; most JSON configs do not). For example, for a client that
   reads an `mcpServers` map (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI):

   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "iphone-use": {
         "command": "/Users/<user>/Applications/iPhoneUse.app/Contents/MacOS/iphone-use-mcp"
       }
     }
   }
   ```

   Merge this entry into the client's existing file; do not replace other servers. The README's
   "Use it from an agent" section has the file location and format for each client.

6. If the `phone_*` tools are not loaded in the current chat, tell the user to start a new chat (or
   restart the client) so it picks up the server.

## Check that it works

- `iphone-use status` says whether the phone is ready for agents.
- In the client, call `phone_status`, then `phone_elements` to read the screen.

## Undo

`~/.iphone-use/uninstall.sh --dry-run` lists what uninstalling removes; drop `--dry-run` to do it.
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install.sh — install iPhoneUse.app and register the GUI-session LaunchAgent
#
# USAGE (recommended — no auth required; GITHUB_TOKEN not needed for public releases):
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leeguooooo/iphone-use/main/install.sh | sh
#
# Local / dev usage (skip download; supply a pre-built .app):
#   ./install.sh /path/to/iPhoneUse.app
#
# A second phone, driven by its own daemon (#67):
#   ./install.sh --instance NAME --udid <UDID> [--port N] [/path/to/iPhoneUse.app]
#   curl -fsSL .../install.sh | sh -s -- --instance NAME --udid <UDID>
# A named instance gets its own copy of the app, state dir
# (~/.iphone-use/instances/NAME), launchd labels, token and ports. It never
# touches the default instance or the shared app; then run its setup-runner.sh.
#
# Requirements:
#   • Must run as the LOGGED-IN GUI user (not root, not over a bare SSH session).
#   • Aqua (WindowServer) session must be active.
#   • macOS 14 Sonoma or later.
#
set -eu

# Configuration paths are derived immediately below, so reject an unset HOME
# before `set -u` can turn it into an opaque unbound-variable failure.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
    printf 'ERROR: HOME is not set. Run as the logged-in desktop user, not root.\n' >&2
    exit 1
fi
umask 077

# Installs made before the rename set PHONE_REMOTE_*; read them as IPHONE_USE_*
# (the new name wins). Names are [A-Z0-9_], so the eval is safe. Plists
# written by older installers are read the same way (plist_env_get_from).
for _legacy in $(env | sed -n 's/^PHONE_REMOTE_\([A-Z0-9_][A-Z0-9_]*\)=.*/\1/p'); do
    eval "[ -n \"\${IPHONE_USE_${_legacy}+x}\" ] || export IPHONE_USE_${_legacy}=\"\$PHONE_REMOTE_${_legacy}\""
done
unset _legacy
# The runner was WebDriverAgent once: IPHONE_USE_WDA_X is now
# IPHONE_USE_RUNNER_X and WDA_X is IPU_RUNNER_X (the new name wins).
for _legacy in $(env | sed -n 's/^IPHONE_USE_WDA_\([A-Z0-9_][A-Z0-9_]*\)=.*/\1/p'); do
    eval "[ -n \"\${IPHONE_USE_RUNNER_${_legacy}+x}\" ] || export IPHONE_USE_RUNNER_${_legacy}=\"\$IPHONE_USE_WDA_${_legacy}\""
done
for _legacy in $(env | sed -n 's/^WDA_\([A-Z0-9_][A-Z0-9_]*\)=.*/\1/p'); do
    eval "[ -n \"\${IPU_RUNNER_${_legacy}+x}\" ] || export IPU_RUNNER_${_legacy}=\"\$WDA_${_legacy}\""
done
unset _legacy

# ── Inline ad-hoc signer ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Direct mode uses this only when the supplied app has no valid signature. It
# creates no certificate and never changes the user's keychain search list.
#
# Order matters and is not obvious: `iphone-use` is the bundle's MAIN
# executable, so codesign treats signing it as signing the bundle and validates
# nested code as it goes. With `iphone-use-mcp` still only linker-signed at
# that point, that validation fails with "code object is not signed at all /
# In subcomponent: .../iphone-use-mcp" and the whole install rolls back. The
# nested helper must be signed BEFORE anything that pulls in bundle
# validation. Covered by scripts/test-install-adhoc-signing.sh.
_inline_sign() {
    local app="$1"
    codesign --force --sign - "$app/Contents/MacOS/iphone-use-mcp"
    if [ -f "$app/Contents/MacOS/iphone-use-legacy-launch" ]; then
        codesign --force --sign - "$app/Contents/MacOS/iphone-use-legacy-launch"
    fi
    codesign --force --sign - "$app/Contents/MacOS/iphone-use"
    codesign --force --sign - "$app"
    ok "Ad-hoc signed without creating a certificate or changing keychain state"
}

# ── Configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BUNDLE_ID="com.leeguoo.iphone-use"
APP_NAME="iPhoneUse.app"
INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/Applications"
PLIST_LABEL="com.leeguoo.iphone-use"
PLIST_DST="$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/${PLIST_LABEL}.plist"
OLD_PLIST_LABEL="work.pwtk.iphone-remote"
OLD_PLIST="$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/${OLD_PLIST_LABEL}.plist"
IPU_RUNNER_PLIST_LABEL="${PLIST_LABEL}.runner"
IPU_RUNNER_PLIST_DST="$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/${IPU_RUNNER_PLIST_LABEL}.plist"
# Before v0.20 the supervisor was ${PLIST_LABEL}.wda; retire_pre_rename_runner
# moves it once the install commits, so its settings are read from there until then.
PRE_RENAME_RUNNER_PLIST="$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/${PLIST_LABEL}.wda.plist"
RUNNER_SETTINGS_PLIST="$IPU_RUNNER_PLIST_DST"
if [ ! -f "$RUNNER_SETTINGS_PLIST" ] && [ -f "$PRE_RENAME_RUNNER_PLIST" ]; then
    RUNNER_SETTINGS_PLIST="$PRE_RENAME_RUNNER_PLIST"
fi
LOG_DIR="$HOME/Library/Logs/iPhoneUse"
REPO="leeguooooo/iphone-use"
BINARY_INSIDE_APP="Contents/MacOS/iphone-use"
MCP_BINARY_INSIDE_APP="Contents/MacOS/iphone-use-mcp"

# --instance/--udid/--port select a named instance; --simulator NAME starts
# that iOS Simulator after the install (preview); anything else is the
# optional local app path, as before.
INSTANCE_NAME="default"
INSTANCE_UDID=""
INSTANCE_PORT=""
INSTALL_ARGS=()
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --instance|--udid|--port|--simulator)
            if [ "$#" -lt 2 ] || [ -z "$2" ]; then
                printf 'ERROR: %s requires a value\n' "$1" >&2
                exit 2
            fi
            case "$2" in
                -*)
                    printf "ERROR: %s requires a value, got the option '%s'\n" "$1" "$2" >&2
                    exit 2
                    ;;
            esac
            case "$1" in
                --instance) INSTANCE_NAME="$2" ;;
                --udid) INSTANCE_UDID="$2" ;;
                --port) INSTANCE_PORT="$2" ;;
                # Exported so the pinned inner installer sees it too.
                --simulator) export IPHONE_USE_SETUP_SIMULATOR="$2" ;;
            esac
            shift 2
            ;;
        --no-setup)
            # Exported so the pinned inner installer sees it too.
            export IPHONE_USE_NO_SETUP=1
            shift
            ;;
        --no-auto-update)
            export IPHONE_USE_AUTO_UPDATE=0
            shift
            ;;
        -*)
            # Not an app path. The common way to get here is a caller that
            # kept options in one variable and expanded it unquoted under
            # zsh, which does not word-split: `sh -s -- $a` then passes
            # "--instance ix --udid …" as ONE argument. Treating it as an app
            # path used to fail later with a misleading "local app path"
            # error; name the real problem before anything is touched.
            case "$1" in
                *" "*)
                    printf "ERROR: '%s' arrived as one argument; each option and its value must be separate arguments.\n" "$1" >&2
                    printf '       zsh does not word-split $var: use ${=var}, an array, or write the options out.\n' >&2
                    ;;
                *)
                    printf "ERROR: unknown option '%s' (accepted: --instance NAME, --udid UDID, --port N, --simulator NAME, --no-setup, --no-auto-update, [app path]).\n" "$1" >&2
                    ;;
            esac
            exit 2
            ;;
        *)
            INSTALL_ARGS+=("$1")
            shift
            ;;
    esac
done
set -- ${INSTALL_ARGS[@]+"${INSTALL_ARGS[@]}"}
if [ "$INSTANCE_NAME" = default ] && { [ -n "$INSTANCE_UDID" ] || [ -n "$INSTANCE_PORT" ]; }; then
    printf 'ERROR: --udid/--port are accepted only with --instance NAME\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi

# commonly names the shell, so deriving `./scripts/...` from it would allow the
# caller's current working directory to inject helpers into `curl | sh`.
SCRIPT_SOURCE="${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}"
SCRIPT_IS_LOCAL=0
SCRIPT_DIR=""
case "$SCRIPT_SOURCE" in
    ""|"-"|/dev/fd/*|/proc/*) ;;
    *)
        if [ "$SCRIPT_SOURCE" = "$0" ] && [ -f "$SCRIPT_SOURCE" ]; then
            SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SCRIPT_SOURCE")" 2>/dev/null && pwd || true)"
            [ -z "$SCRIPT_DIR" ] || SCRIPT_IS_LOCAL=1
        fi
        ;;
esac

BOOTSTRAP_TMP=""
SIGN_SH_DL=""
APP_STAGE=""

# other file there belongs to someone else and is left alone. The link target
# is the stable app path, so an upgrade or rollback never leaves it dangling.
# Runs after the daemon transaction commits; a failure here only warns.
install_cli_link() {
    local target="$1"
    local dir="${IPHONE_USE_BIN_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"
    local link="$dir/iphone-use"
    local current
    if [ -L "$link" ]; then
        current="$(readlink "$link" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        case "$current" in
            "$target") ;;
            */iPhoneUse.app/Contents/MacOS/iphone-use) ;;
            *)
                warn "Left $link alone: it points at ${current:-an unreadable target}, not iphone-use."
                info "Run the CLI as: $target"
                return 0
                ;;
        esac
    elif [ -e "$link" ]; then
        warn "Left $link alone: it is not a link this installer made."
        info "Run the CLI as: $target"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "${current:-}" != "$target" ]; then
        if ! (umask 022 && mkdir -p "$dir") 2>/dev/null \
            || ! ln -sfn "$target" "$link" 2>/dev/null; then
            warn "Could not link $link; run the CLI as: $target"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    ok "Command line: $link -> $target"
    case ":${PATH:-}:" in
        *":$dir:"*) ;;
        *) warn "$dir is not on PATH; add it to use \`iphone-use upgrade\` (or run $target)." ;;
    esac
    return 0
}

# USB-attached iPhones, by UDID, straight from usbmuxd (no extra tools).
usb_iphones() {
    python3 - 2>/dev/null <<'PY'
import socket, struct, plistlib
try:
    s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM); s.settimeout(3)
    s.connect("/var/run/usbmuxd")
    p = plistlib.dumps({"MessageType": "ListDevices", "ClientVersionString": "x", "ProgName": "x"})
    s.sendall(struct.pack("<IIII", len(p) + 16, 1, 8, 1) + p)
    h = s.recv(16); n = struct.unpack("<I", h[:4])[0]; d = b""
    while len(d) < n - 16:
        d += s.recv(n - 16 - len(d))
    devices = plistlib.loads(d).get("DeviceList", [])
    print(" ".join(sorted({x["Properties"]["SerialNumber"] for x in devices
                           if x["Properties"].get("ConnectionType") == "USB"})))
except Exception:
    pass
PY

# Sets FIRST_SETUP_DONE=1 when setup and the demo both succeeded.

first_run_setup() {
    local cli="$1" wanted="$2" usb rerun="iphone-use setup"
    shift 2
    [ "$#" -eq 0 ] || rerun="$rerun $*"
    echo ""
    printf '%b━━━ Set up the iPhone ━━━%b\n' "$BOLD" "$RESET"
    if [ "${IPHONE_USE_NO_SETUP:-0}" = "1" ]; then

        return 0

    usb="$(usb_iphones)"
    if [ -z "$usb" ] || { [ -n "$wanted" ] && case " $usb " in *" $wanted "*) false ;; *) true ;; esac; }; then
        info "Plug the iPhone in with a cable, unlock it, then run: $rerun"
        info "No phone at hand? Drive an iOS Simulator instead (preview, needs Xcode): iphone-use simulator start \"iPhone 16 Pro\""
        return 0

    info "An iPhone is plugged in; setting it up now (keep it unlocked; the first build takes a few minutes)."

# simulator_setup <cli> <mcp-binary>
# --simulator NAME / IPHONE_USE_SETUP_SIMULATOR=NAME (preview): start that
# simulator with the runner and a daemon (instance `sim`) and register an
# iphone-sim MCP server for it. It was asked for, so it also runs without a
# terminal (CI) and on upgrades, and a failure fails the install.
simulator_setup() {
    local cli="$1" mcp="$2" name="${IPHONE_USE_SETUP_SIMULATOR:-}"
    echo ""
    printf '%b━━━ Set up the simulator ━━━%b\n' "$BOLD" "$RESET"

# register_claude_mcp <mcp-binary> <server-name> [instance]
# The bare command is enough: the MCP server reads its daemon URL and token
# from the daemon's own LaunchAgent, so no secret lands in Claude's config.
register_claude_mcp() {
    local mcp="$1" name="$2" instance="${3:-}" existing json
    command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
        info "MCP command for agents: $mcp${instance:+ (env IPHONE_USE_INSTANCE=$instance)}"
        return 0
    }
    if existing="$(claude mcp get "$name" 2>/dev/null)"; then
        if printf '%s' "$existing" | grep -qF "$mcp"; then
            ok "Claude Code already has the $name MCP server."
        else
            warn "Claude Code already has an MCP server named $name with another command; left it unchanged."
        fi
        return 0
    fi
    if [ -n "$instance" ]; then
        json="$(printf '{"type":"stdio","command":"%s","args":[],"env":{"IPHONE_USE_INSTANCE":"%s"}}' "$mcp" "$instance")"
    else
        json="$(printf '{"type":"stdio","command":"%s","args":[]}' "$mcp")"
    fi
    if claude mcp add-json -s user "$name" "$json" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ok "Claude Code can now use the iPhone (MCP server \"$name\"). Undo: claude mcp remove -s user $name"
    else
        warn "Could not register the MCP server with Claude Code; add it by hand: claude mcp add -s user $name -- $mcp"
    fi
}

# register_codex_mcp <mcp-binary> <server-name> [instance]
# Same for the Codex CLI (~/.codex/config.toml). The name matches the one the
# Codex plugin ships, so a plugin install and this entry stay one tool set.
register_codex_mcp() {
    local mcp="$1" name="$2" instance="${3:-}" existing current
    command -v codex >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
    if existing="$(codex mcp get "$name" --json 2>/dev/null)"; then
        # "<command>\t<IPHONE_USE_INSTANCE or empty>" of the existing entry.
        current="$(printf '%s' "$existing" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
t = json.load(sys.stdin).get("transport") or {}
print("%s\t%s" % (t.get("command") or "", (t.get("env") or {}).get("IPHONE_USE_INSTANCE") or ""))
' 2>/dev/null)" || current=""
        if [ "$current" = "$mcp	$instance" ]; then
            ok "Codex already has the $name MCP server."
            return 0
        fi
        if [ -z "$instance" ] \
            && printf '%s' "$existing" | grep -qF "\$HOME/Applications/$APP_NAME/$MCP_BINARY_INSIDE_APP"; then
            # The plugin's launcher: the default daemon, which is this install.
            ok "Codex already has the $name MCP server (from the iPhone Use plugin)."
            return 0
        fi
        if [ "${current%%	*}" != "$mcp" ]; then
            warn "Codex already has an MCP server named $name with another command; left it unchanged."
            return 0
        fi
        # Our binary aimed at the wrong phone (instance env missing or
        # different): replace it so $name drives this instance.
        if ! codex mcp remove "$name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            warn "Codex's $name MCP server does not target instance ${instance:-default}; fix it by hand: codex mcp remove $name"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    if [ -n "$instance" ]; then
        set -- codex mcp add "$name" --env "IPHONE_USE_INSTANCE=$instance" -- "$mcp"
    else
        set -- codex mcp add "$name" -- "$mcp"
    fi
    if "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ok "Codex can now use the iPhone (MCP server \"$name\"). Undo: codex mcp remove $name"
    else
        warn "Could not register the MCP server with Codex; add it by hand: $*"
    fi
}

register_json_mcp() {

    [ "${IPHONE_USE_NO_CLIENT_SETUP:-0}" = "1" ] && return 0
    [ -d "$(dirname "$file")" ] || return 0
    command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
    python3 - "$file" "$mcp" "$name" "$instance" 2>/dev/null <<'PY' || rc=$?
import json, os, shutil, sys, tempfile
path, mcp, name, instance = sys.argv[1:5]
path = os.path.realpath(path)  # a symlinked config keeps its link
cfg = {}
if os.path.exists(path):
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            text = f.read()
        cfg = json.loads(text) if text.strip() else {}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        sys.exit(5)
if not isinstance(cfg, dict):
    sys.exit(5)
servers = cfg.setdefault("mcpServers", {})
if not isinstance(servers, dict):
    sys.exit(5)
entry = {"command": mcp, "args": []}
if instance:
    entry["env"] = {"IPHONE_USE_INSTANCE": instance}
old = servers.get(name)
if old is not None:
    same = isinstance(old, dict) and old.get("command") == mcp \
        and ((old.get("env") or {}).get("IPHONE_USE_INSTANCE") or "") == instance
    sys.exit(3 if same else 4)
servers[name] = entry
if os.path.exists(path):
    shutil.copy2(path, path + ".iphone-use.bak")
fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=os.path.dirname(path), prefix=".iphone-use.")
try:
    with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(cfg, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
        f.write("\n")
    if os.path.exists(path):
        shutil.copymode(path, tmp)
    os.replace(tmp, path)
except BaseException:
    os.unlink(tmp)
    raise
PY
    case "$rc" in
        0) ok "$client can now use the iPhone (MCP server \"$name\" in $file; restart $client). Undo: remove \"$name\" from that file" ;;
        3) ok "$client already has the $name MCP server." ;;
        4) warn "$client already has an MCP server named $name with another command; left it unchanged." ;;

# iphone-use — drive a real iPhone

The [iphone-use](https://github.com/leeguooooo/iphone-use) daemon drives a
physical iPhone through its own XCTest device runner. This runner replaced
WebDriverAgent in v0.14.0; it does not use iPhone Mirroring. The HTTP interface
is WebDriverAgent-compatible (its `/wda/...` routes). It never touches the Mac's screen or
cursor. Use the HTTP API below or the bundled MCP server (`phone_*` tools); the
loop is the same. Details live in the reference: `curl -s -H "$AUTH"
"$HOST/agent/reference"` serves the copy that matches the running daemon
(sections below are named by heading; also
[docs/agent-reference.md](https://github.com/leeguooooo/iphone-use/blob/main/docs/agent-reference.md)).

```bash
HOST="${IPHONE_USE_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:44321}"
AUTH="Authorization: Bearer $IPHONE_USE_TOKEN"   # daemon password or IPHONE_USE_AGENT_TOKEN
MUTATION="X-Phone-Control: 1"                      # required on every state-changing POST
OWNER="X-Phone-Owner: <your-session-name>"          # MCP sends this for you
curl -s -H "$AUTH" "$HOST/agent/status"             # probe first; on failure follow recovery below
```

## The loop

1. **Probe.** If the user names a phone or multiple phones are installed, first
   use `phone_instances`, then pass that `instance` on every MCP read/action.
   Omitted instance reports only the configured daemon, never all phones.
   `GET /agent/status` / `phone_status`. Screen reads and UI input
   require `drivable:true`; otherwise pause those operations and follow the recovery steps below.
   Paired metadata reads (`phone_home_layout`, `phone_apps`) and cached capability
   discovery do not require a running Runner. Use them without reconnecting or
   opening Home, and respect any private-hold refusal. Reconnect once
   (`phone_reconnect`, with `wait_secs` to block until drivable or a blocker /
   `POST /agent/mode {"mode":"agent"}`) only when the
   user's current task needs the phone, never for a health check: each runner
   launch can make the operator type the passcode. If `owner` is another
   session, do not drive. → reference: *Phone states and recovery*

2. **Look for a saved flow first.** Entering an app — a `launch_app` response,
   or the first `/agent/elements` read in a newly entered app — carries a
   `registry` block listing the saved flows for it. If one does the task, run
   it with `phone_flow_run`: one call instead of dozens, no screenshots.
   `phone_flow_list` / `iphone-use-mcp flow list --app <bundle>` shows them
   all. Check `risk` and `compat` before running. → reference: *Flows*

   ```bash
   "$HOME/Applications/iPhoneUse.app/Contents/MacOS/iphone-use-mcp" flow run system/spotlight-search --input query=Health
   ```

3. **No flow? Hand a clear goal to Jev.** `phone_jev_run` /
   `iphone-use-mcp jev run --goal "…" [--app <bundle>]` runs a fast on-phone
   agent (TypeSafe's Jev picks each step, ~1–2 s/step, no model turns) and
   returns `done` / `blocked` with its step history. Confirm goals that send,
   pay or delete with the user first; check the end screen yourself.

4. **Otherwise act in batches, not taps.** Every call costs you a full turn;
   the phone takes ~0.5 s. Open the app with `launch_app`, read
   `GET /agent/elements` once, then send everything you can already see how to
   do as ONE batch (`POST /agent/actions` / `phone_run_steps`, up to 24 steps,
   `wait_for` after each screen change) with `observe:true` (MCP default): the
   reply carries the screen the batch ended on, so you decide the next batch
   without another read. If you will think between batches for more than a
   minute, `phone_hold` keeps the runner from being released. Single taps (element + snapshot, unique label,
   locator) are for exploring a screen you have not read yet; after three in a
   row the daemon says so (`batch_hint`).

5. **Verify** each step against your postcondition: MCP act tools observe by
   default (HTTP: `?return=delta`) and return the settled change in the same
   call; the settled screen is captured too, and `phone_screenshot` returns it
   instantly — look only when the text is not enough. `ok:true` means
   the action was sent, not that it achieved anything.
   → reference: *Reading results*

6. **Offer to save it.** When a response carries `flow_suggestion`, or you
   finish a multi-step task that no flow covered, **ask the user** whether to
   keep it as a flow. Only if they agree: get the draft
   (`phone_flow_draft(save_as=…)` / `flow draft --out …` /
   `GET /agent/flow/draft`), fix its `todo` list, validate it, and run the file
   once. Publishing opens a public PR, so ask again before
   `phone_flow_publish(confirm=true)`. → reference: *Saving a flow*

When the task is done, release the phone: `phone_release_owner` /
`POST /agent/owner {"release":true}`. If a response carried `agent_focus`, the
phone is on Do Not Disturb for your session: tell the user, and releasing turns
it off again.
